stem: A nurse is providing oral care to an unconscious client. Which positioning action best reduces aspiration risk during the procedure?

options.A: Elevate the head to at least about 45 degrees and turn the head to the side
options.B: Keep the client flat and supine with the head in midline
options.C: Place the client in Trendelenburg position
options.D: Position the client prone with the face directed into the mattress

rationale: NCBI StatPearls guidance for oral hygiene in an unconscious patient recommends elevating the head to about 45 degrees or more and turning the head to the side. This positioning helps oral fluid and secretions drain away from the airway while oral care is performed. A flat supine position increases aspiration risk in a client who cannot protect the airway.
educational_objective: Position an unconscious client for oral care with the head elevated and turned laterally to reduce aspiration risk.
source_locator: Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions > Dental Care > unconscious patient
source_claim_supported: For oral care in an unconscious patient, elevate the head to 45 degrees or more and turn it to the side to facilitate safe oral hygiene and reduce aspiration risk.
correction_summary: Replaced the over-specific requirement for full side-lying with the directly supported positioning instruction: head elevated at least about 45 degrees and turned to the side. Removed conversational cueing from distractors.
audit_findings: A directly matches the NCBI procedure. B leaves an unprotected airway dependent; C and D are not recommended oral-care positions. No second answer remains.
